questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Slap on the wrist
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4 - A mild punishment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Slap on the wrist" **is an **idiom** that means** to give a mild punishment or a reprimand for a wrongdoing.** It is not a severe punishment, but rather a warning or a reminder to the person to behave better in the future.

 
 
• Example: The teacher gave the student** a slap on the wrist** for not completing his homework on time.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **1) Wild with excitement **- This means to be very excited or enthusiastic about something.
 
 
• Example: The children were wild with excitement when they saw the circus animals.
 
 
 
• **2) Misunderstand each other** - This means to not understand each other's words or actions correctly.
 
 
• Example: The two friends had a misunderstanding and stopped talking to each other.
 
 
 
• **3) Criticize someone strongly and angrily **- This means to express disapproval or dissatisfaction with someone's behavior in a harsh manner.
 
 
• Example: The boss criticized the employee strongly and angrily for not meeting the deadline.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Ace in the hole

options.text: To create noisy disturbances so that competitors are unable to work.
A major advantage that one keeps hidden until an ideal time.
To attempt to do the impossible.
To suffer an injury on the lower body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A major advantage that one keeps hidden until an ideal time**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Ace in the hole"** is an idiomatic expression that originated from poker, specifically stud poker. In stud poker, each player receives some cards face-up and others face-down. The face-down cards are called "hole cards." The "ace" is the highest-ranking card in many card games.
 
• The idiom "Ace in the hole" figuratively refers to a hidden advantage or resource that a person keeps secret until the right moment.
 
• It represents a powerful tool or strategy that can be revealed when needed to gain a significant advantage over others. This advantage is typically withheld or kept in reserve until an opportune time arises, maximizing its impact and effectiveness.

Therefore, the correct meaning of the idiom "Ace in the hole" is:** A major advantage that one keeps hidden until an ideal time**.
